summary:
I applied the look checker's fixes and its relief changes to the default slate tile. Only settings changed: recipe/settings.json went from 49 to 65 entries, and no layer file or recipe code was edited. I baked the finished tile again at 1254 dots into outputs/default/ (colour, 16-bit height, normal at strength 7, roughness, metallic) and checked it by eye, by the look measures and by both scores.

How it looks now, next to the reference:
- The paint is in broader, flatter bands, and the fine liquified ripple is mostly gone.
- There is about the reference's amount of moss (olive 6.0% against 6.4%). It is mottled dark and light instead of a flat khaki stain, with no rows of teeth.
- The big tan L-shaped corner chips are gone. A pale broken lip and small flecks now run along the lower edges (tan 1.03% against 1.0%).
- The lower corners are rounder and the row shadow is a cleaner two-step band. There are no black drips, no hair-like crack and fewer lichen dots.
- The pale outlier slates are less loud (brightest slate 36.8, was 38.9; the reference's brightest is 34.6).
- Under the raking light the tile looks less like rippled planks, but it is still flatter than the reference.

Scores:
- Overall went from 0.705 to 0.730, and the colour group from 0.701 to 0.755.
- Almost all of the colour gain comes from the fragile feature-size measure. Without it the colour group is flat (0.767 before, 0.764 after).
- Height group went from 0.654 to 0.649 and normal group from 0.671 to 0.678.

What I did not take from the verdict:
- I kept combine.tone_blend at 0.7 instead of the suggested 0.45. At 0.45 the slates looked flatter, both slope measures moved away from the reference, and the overall score dropped to 0.693.
- I kept the other three relief changes (lip_height 0.1, sink_depth 1.6, moss.raise 2.5).
- Problem 5 is only partly fixed: the level edges (lips, chips) still carry less relief than in the reference.

New small faults:
- Faint horizontal contour lines show under the raking light. With the broader bands, the steps of the fade down each slate become long wavy lines.
- The tile is slightly darker and bluer than before (mean Lab 24.2/-1.7/-1.7 against the reference's 25.2/-1.6/-1.0). Before, the extra moss hid this.
- I tried raising colour_and_fade.tone_centre to fix the darkness, but it brought the pale slate back and the colour score fell. I set it back.

Problem 11 (moss cut straight at the side joints) could not be fixed with settings; it would need a code change in moss.py, which I did not try. I used 14 of about 18 Blender runs, and the slate_layers folder is 413 MB.

On your question about the other textures: lit_several.py (the raking-light check) works on any surface as it is, and views.py works on any pictures. In measure_look.py the gradient, stripe and relief measures work on any surface, but the olive, tan, moss and brightest-slate measures only fit slate. bake_variants.py and make_pictures.py point at the slate folders and would need their paths changed.

settings_changes.name: moss.edge_raggedness

settings_changes.name: layout.ragged_bottom
settings_changes.why: Problem 4: more uneven lower edges.

settings_changes.name: outline_and_shadow.black_drips

settings_changes.why: Problem 8: the lone hair-like crack is gone.

settings_changes.name: outline_and_shadow.lip_height
settings_changes.why: Problem 5: the lip and chipped lower edge catch more light. Raises the up-down slope a little and gave the best height and normal scores of the relief options tried.

settings_changes.name: damage.sink_depth
settings_changes.why: Problem 5: chips sit deeper.

settings_changes.name: moss.raise
settings_changes.why: Problem 5: moss stands up a little.

settings_changes.name: combine.tone_blend
settings_changes.why: Problem 5 suggestion. At 0.45 the slates looked flatter under the raking light. Up-down and side slopes moved away from the reference (9.44 to 9.06 and 12.04 to 11.52 at 900 dots; reference 11.57 and 12.90). At 1254 dots the overall score was 0.693 (height 0.602, normal 0.567) against 0.724 when 0.7 is kept with the other three relief changes. 0.55 was also tried and was in between.

settings_changes.name: outline_and_shadow.shadow_tiers
settings_changes.why: Problem 6: the shadow reads as a cleaner dark band with fewer stepped tiers. Olive share drops 0.4 points where the band covers moss tops.

settings_changes.name: colour_and_fade.outlier_size
settings_changes.why: Problem 7: brightest slate 38.0 to 36.8 (reference 34.6); the pale slate is less loud.

settings_changes.name: colour_and_fade.outlier_share
settings_changes.why: Problem 7: the brightest slate did not change (38.0), so the brightest slates are not outliers.

settings_changes.name: damage.side_share
settings_changes.why: Only 0.036% of dots changed; invisible once corner_gain is 0.3.

settings_changes.name: layout.bottom_tilt
settings_changes.why: Problem 4: 0.035 made no visible change (row wander 3.96 to 4.00). 0.06 gives small steps between neighbouring lower edges; my rough row-wander measure goes 3.83 to 4.09 dots (reference 5.0).

settings_changes.name: moss.tone_1
settings_changes.why: Wider moss palette (darker end): lightness spread inside the moss 4.3 to 5.8-6.0 (reference 6.0).

settings_changes.name: moss.tone_5
settings_changes.why: Wider moss palette (lighter end).

settings_changes.name: moss.tone_centre
settings_changes.why: With the wider palette alone the moss was too light (mean L 31.6 against 29.4). At 0.55: mean L 28.9, spread 5.9. 0.45 was also tried and dropped (too dark, olive 4.4%).

settings_changes.name: moss.joint_preference
settings_changes.why: Try at problem 11. Olive fell 5.8 to 5.2% and the straight cut at the joint remained.

settings_changes.name: damage.chip_amount
settings_changes.why: After step (a) the tan share was too low (0.79% against 1.0%). 0.8 overshot (1.34%), so I chose a value in between. The final tile has 1.03% at 900 dots.

settings_changes.name: outline_and_shadow.lip_breakup
settings_changes.why: Lip slightly more broken by eye, but the stripe measure moved 1.00 to 1.04, away from the reference's 0.83.

settings_changes.name: colour_and_fade.tone_centre
settings_changes.why: Tried to undo the darker overall colour. Mean L went 24.2 to 24.7 / 25.3 (reference 25.2), but the brightest slate rose to 37.2 / 37.5. Baked at 1254, 3.85 dropped the colour group to 0.692 and overall to 0.703 (feature-size measure 0.722 to 0.419). Reverted and re-baked.

code_changes: No layer file or recipe code changed. The only recipe change is recipe/settings.json, 49 to 65 entries (31 changed or added; listed in look_fixes/set_final.json).

New in proc-work/recipes/slate_layers/look_fixes/: measure_look.py (the look checker's measures, calibrated; has a reference@SIZE option), bake_variants.py (several settings variants in one Blender run, using the harness's own scene), lit_several.py (the checker's raking-light scene for several tiles in one run), views.py (side-by-side pictures) and make_pictures.py (the four before/after pictures).

Saved the starting point: recipe/settings_before_look_fixes.json and outputs/default_before_look_fixes/ (colour, height, normal, roughness, metallic, bake.json, both score JSONs). Neither was changed afterwards.

outputs/default/ was replaced by the new 1254 bake. normal.png is now the strength-7 normal from integration/make_normal.py; the harness's own normal was renamed normal_harness_sobel.png. score_same_kind.json, score_pixel_for_transparency.json, sheet_same_kind.jpg and log.txt were rewritten.

scores_text:
Same-kind scores (lib/texture_compare.py against slate; the before was re-scored the same way and matched the stored numbers):

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| overall | 0.705 | 0.730 |
| colour group | 0.701 | 0.755 |
| - colour distribution | 0.926 | 0.890 |
| - colour spectrum | 0.609 | 0.541 |
| - colour orientation | 0.630 | 0.742 |
| - colour scale | 0.452 | 0.722 |
| - colour gradient | 0.753 | 0.826 |
| height group | 0.654 | 0.649 |
| normal group | 0.671 | 0.678 |
| tiling | 1.0 | 1.0 |

Almost all of the colour-group gain is the feature-size (colour scale) measure, which jumps easily: with colour_and_fade.tone_centre 3.85 it fell back to 0.419 (colour 0.692, overall 0.703). Without that measure the colour group is 0.767 before and 0.764 after.

Pixel numbers (lib/pixel_compare.py), for transparency only:
- Delta E 10.45 to 10.15
- SSIM 0.530 to 0.549
- edge skill 0.167 to 0.150
- height error after best fit 37.7 to 37.6
- normal angle 16.9 to 16.3 degrees
- tier: none (unchanged)

Score files: proc-work/recipes/slate_layers/outputs/default/score_same_kind.json and score_pixel_for_transparency.json.
untested: Other seeds: everything was tuned on the default seeds only; the seed alone moves the colour group by about 0.07.
Not re-baked, as the task said: the 8 variations, seed spread, 2x2 and 4x4 areas, ladder and guides. They still show the OLD default look. Problem 10 (the variations' own settings) was not touched.
Independence and half-tile tests: not re-run, because no layer file changed. The new tile's seam score is 1.0.
Only the checker's single raking-light direction, at the whole tile and one 0.4-tile window. No 3D roof render.
Problem 11 (moss cut straight at side joints): no settings change fixed it; the code fix (fading growth near side edges in layers/moss.py) was not tried.
Unsure whether layout.bottom_tilt 0.06 reads better to other eyes (a small change), and whether 0.72 is the best damage.chip_amount (picked between two tested values).

Outside my folders, so not edited: recipe/controls.md (its default column now disagrees with settings.json; rebuild with recipe/make_controls_table.py), and the 05 Recipe guide, the README and final_report.json (they still quote the old default's 0.705).

Could not reproduce some of the checker's numbers: the slate-to-slate spread (mine 3.84, checker 3.6) and the row-band wander and solid-black share (mine 3.2 against 5.0 dots and 100% against 89-94%; checker 4.4 against 5.7 and 95% against 85%). The olive and tan colour rules are my guesses that reproduce the checker's shares, not necessarily its code.
failures: My first Blender command failed straight away with 'blender: command not found' (Blender is not on the PATH); nothing ran. After that I used /home/user/work/blender-app/blender-5.2.2-linux-x64/blender.

The colour_and_fade.tone_centre 3.85 trial (to fix the darker overall colour) lowered the colour score to 0.692 and raised the brightest slate. Reverting it cost a third 1254 bake; the trial and revert together took 4 of the 14 Blender runs.
One waiting command hit the 10-minute foreground limit and moved to the background. It finished correctly.
Problem 5 is only partly fixed: the level-edge slope fell (11.2 to 10.3; reference 13.5) even though the tilt and the up-down to side balance improved.
New small faults: faint horizontal contour lines across some slates under the raking light, and a slightly darker, bluer overall colour (mean Lab 24.2/-1.7/-1.7 against 25.2/-1.6/-1.0).
